pairs.question: Quae noxam magna tulere iurgia? quis uestro deus interuenit amori?
pairs.answer: Phyllide contentus sola (tu testis, Iolla) Callirhoen spreui, quamuis cum dote rogaret: en, sibi cum Mopso calamos intexere cera incipit et puero comitata sub ilice cantat.
pairs.derivation: Iollas asks Lycidas what quarrel caused the trouble and what god intervened in his love. Dropped the speech-framing 'nunc age dic, Lycida:' which narrates the asking, leaving the two interrogative sentences as the question (normalized capital Q). Lycidas's reply directly answers the cause: content with Phyllis alone he had spurned Callirhoe, but then saw Phyllis making music with Mopsus. Answer ends at the first full stop after the question ('...cantat.', line 231); cut before line 232 'haec ego cum uidi...', which turns from explaining the cause to recounting his own reaction (tearing his garments), i.e. elaboration rather than answer.
